Targeted correction: the three enlarged flower shadows on the blue-gray wall currently contain warm, pale stamen-like lines at their centers. Remove those lit details completely from every projected flower shadow. These wall shadows must be credible dark occlusion silhouettes: wall texture may show through their dark values, but there must be no illuminated stamens, colored flower interiors, white petal surfaces, warm highlights, or bright internal floral details inside the projected shapes. The warm stamens and soft white petals belong exclusively to the three real, illuminated flowers at the lower left.

Where needed, refine the projected petal and leaf outlines to correspond to the actual lower-left plant's visible blossoms, branching stems and leaf shapes. Preserve the count and spatial order of the three real flowers and three enlarged projected flower heads. Preserve one continuous cast presence back to the real rooted base, upward-right projection, enlargement, and softening with distance under the existing single low light from the lower left. Avoid inventing a second light or turning the shadow into a drawing of another lit plant.

Keep the real plant unchanged: all three real flowers, actual stamens, petal forms, leaves, stem branching, scale, positions and warm illumination. Keep the rooted soil contact, wall-to-ground contact, real wall texture and photographic character. Preserve the source's overall crop, composition, blue-gray nighttime colors, lower-left illumination, darkness progression, ground strip, and all other image areas as closely as possible.
Preserve the title's exact location, scale, bold Korean sans-serif style, pale color, one horizontal line, complete intact strokes and two visible word spaces. The only printed text, exactly once, verbatim: 밤에 피는 정원
No additional copy, symbols, marks, logos or watermarks. Do not move or restyle the title. Do not add props, flowers, lamps, halos, stars, moon, spotlight graphics, decorative effects, frames or panels. The correction is localized to the projected shadows, especially their falsely lit centers.
